title: Probability: the Fundamental Counting Principle and Arrangements
seo_title: Grade 12 Counting and Probability Worksheets with Answers (CAPS Maths)
standard_text: Generalisation of the fundamental counting principle; probability problems using the fundamental counting principle; factorial notation; arrangements with and without repetition.
meta_desc: Free CAPS Grade 12 probability worksheets: the fundamental counting principle, factorials, codes, arrangements of letters and probability. 100 questions with memos.
key_sub: Repeated letters: divide by their factorials.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • Fundamental counting principle: if one choice can be made in m ways and the next in n ways, together there are m × n ways.
  • n objects in a row: n! = n × (n − 1) × … × 1.
  • With repeated letters, divide by the factorial of each repeat.
  • Probability = number of favourable arrangementstotal number of arrangements.

Examples

Example

BANANA

6! ÷ (3! × 2!)

Answer: 60

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
AddingMultiply the choices.
RepetitionWithout repetition, the choices go down.
Repeated lettersDivide by the repeats.

items.q: A committee of 4 is chosen at random from 12 people, including Zinhle and Jabu. What is the probability that both Zinhle and Jabu are chosen?
items.e: Ways that include both: 10C2 = 45. All committees: 12C4 = 495. 45/495 = 111.

items.q: 4 books, including a dictionary and an atlas, are placed on a shelf in random order. What is the probability that the dictionary is first and the atlas is second?
items.e: Arrangements with those two fixed: 2! = 2. All arrangements: 4! = 24. 112.
